+<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
+
+# Resolve native dictionary views before the fused group consumer
+
+Status: historical revision-three correction, subsequently removed with the
+maintainer-requested [whole-item drop](../benchmarks/native-workflow-drop-2026-10-25.md).
+The following records its original premeasurement rationale.
+The [original finite protocol](native-fused-measure-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md)
+continues to own admission, correctness, six immutable inputs, resource grants,
+paired schedule, timing thresholds and package acceptance. This note records
+the exact change after its revision-two observation gate failed.
+
+## Preserved failure and source diagnosis
+
+All twelve revision-two debug calls completed with exact ordered values,
+schemas, resource cleanup and expected computed-column elimination. The
+independent verifier rejected the candidate because all three dictionary
+targets observed zero dictionary-backed domains. No revision-two release
+measurement ran, and no timing benefit is inferred from debug execution.
+The first parsing failure remains separate and unchanged.
+
+The immutable files retain their dictionaries. A small program linked against
+the pinned Vortex 0.90.0 build reproduces the composed scan projection and
+selection: the selected key is a deferred `get_item` over `select`, with the
+dictionary below it. The existing variable-key owner checks the outer array
+for `Dict` before requesting `VarBinViewArray`; that request expands the key.
+Vortex's existing `execute_until::<Dict>` resolves the wrapper and stops at
+the dictionary (or an ordinary canonical array). The reproduction checks all
+2,048 selected values, dtype and row count. Its earlier no-projection probe
+is preserved too: it disproved the initial assumption that every filtered
+scan already has this wrapper.
+
+## Candidate boundary and provider decision
+
+Resolve only UTF8/Binary group columns inside the already admitted fused
+consumer. Complete the existing projection preparations in their original
+order first; then use the query's native execution context to resolve the
+group views, check unchanged dtype/rows and pass them to the existing grouping
+owner. Numeric mapping, arithmetic order, source checks, input files, ordinary
+non-admitted execution and spill selection remain unchanged. No provider or
+allocator failure triggers replay, source reopening or a strategy retry.
+
+This is `use_vortex_native_provider`: pinned Vortex 0.90.0 array execution,
+isolated in `shardloom-vortex`, behind the existing local-primitives feature
+and query admission. Existing native I/O and fused-stage certificates report
+the path with `fallback_attempted=false`. There is no new interpreter,
+representation, dependency, worker pool or external engine. Group identity
+uses actual dictionary values, with existing full-domain validation and
+credited native backing owners.
+
+## Revision-three proof, frozen before timing
+
+Keep the identical corrected cost harness and original native inputs in both
+roles. The unchanged baseline reuses its frozen revision-two debug and release
+executables, source overlays and build receipts; verify their hashes before
+and after every cohort. Build and freeze the revised candidate separately.
+Run twelve debug observations before the original 72-call release schedule.
+No failed cohort is replaced or given acceptance credit.
+
+Require the original complete values, schemas, cleanup, absence of fallback,
+CPU and memory controls, exact mapped rows and zero constructed expression
+rows for eligible candidates. In addition, verify delivered scan rows equal
+the independent selected-row count. Each dictionary target must observe one
+dictionary-backed group domain per delivered scan batch and 65 dictionary
+entries per such domain. Plain/high-cardinality and ineligible controls must
+keep zero dictionary-backed domains; tiny uses its eight-entry domain.
+
+The revision-two verifier also required equal variable-domain value counts
+between roles. That auxiliary check measures prepared dictionary entries,
+not source consumption, and is incompatible with the intended encoded
+consumer: dense inputs can shrink that count, while sparse batches can refer
+to fewer rows than the complete dictionary has entries. Revision three
+replaces that equality with the exact dictionary-entry checks above and
+independent delivered-row validation. Preserve equal domain-owner counts.
+This is an explicit mechanism-check correction, not a timing-threshold change.
+The 2% target improvement in both cohorts, 5% engine and first-execution
+controls, and tiny's 50-microsecond allowance remain unchanged. A further
+activation or timing failure ends this revision without silent retries.
+
+Extend the existing dictionary/null/order/reexecution regression to assert
+actual dictionary activation. Recheck native semantics, cancellation, denial,
+cleanup and lint before the isolated comparison. The package still requires
+public-surface proof, broad checks and one isolated standard Full43 before PR."},{"sha":"5096c5e6d16c0207e238fb80cb100a4889c5b863","filename":"docs/architecture/native-fused-measure-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md","status":"added","additions":154,"deletions":0,"changes":154,"blob_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/99d62ae3d10117720206463a27527a936623d182/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-fused-measure-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/raw/99d62ae3d10117720206463a27527a936623d182/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-fused-measure-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/depsilon/shardloom/contents/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-fused-measure-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md?ref=99d62ae3d10117720206463a27527a936623d182","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
+
+# Consume computed integer measures without an intermediate column
+
+Status: historical candidate protocol; the maintainer subsequently drops the
+whole item-15 batch after its combined Full43 checkpoint. The implementation is
+removed; the [drop record](../benchmarks/native-workflow-drop-2026-10-25.md)
+preserves the decision and restored-main check. The protocol below retains its
+original premeasurement scope and earlier failures.
+This is the second mechanism in item 15's workflow work-elimination package.
+The comparison baseline includes the separately retained counted join on merged
+#1605 (`167ac248ba662ae7967a7801995e9b160b17bae5`). RFC 0044 and RFCs
+0013–0017/0021–0022 retain ownership of resources, semantics and execution.
+
+## Existing path and provider decision
+
+The composed native scan/filter/project/aggregate path constructs a full integer
+projection, then prepares that output as an aggregate value column. The proposed
+consumer removes that computed column and prepares its original integer source
+once. It reuses the existing expression arithmetic, exact grouping, ordered
+aggregate updates and finalization. Scanning, predicate evaluation and selected
+input gathering remain unchanged. This makes one concrete intermediate removable
+without changing validation of other filtered columns.
+
+Pinned Vortex 0.90.0 provides the existing ArrayRef, Dict, native primitive,
+validity, take/slice, allocator and file-layout providers. Existing ShardLoom
+KeyColumn/RowSet preserve dictionary equality and full backing ownership.
+The primitive dictionary-partial reducer already serves its own admitted
+workloads; it does not consume this composed projection. Extend the existing
+native consumer, rather than introduce another expression interpreter, key table,
+executor, pool, dependency, or Arrow execution boundary. This is a
+`wrap_vortex_concept` decision with native residual execution and
+`fallback_attempted=false`. Encoding preservation needs actual observations,
+not merely a dictionary-shaped fixture declaration.
+
+## Admission and semantics
+
+Admit a grouped aggregate directly over project → filter → scan, including
+the ordinary binder's equivalent project → scan-with-pushed-predicate shape.
+The projection
+contains only identity group keys (aliases allowed) and exactly one computed
+integer measure, with every output consumed. Measures may be COUNT(*),
+COUNT(computed), SUM(computed), or AVG(computed); at least one consumes the
+computed measure. The expression is one add, subtract or multiply between a
+column and a non-null I64 literal, in either operand order, with I64 output.
+Prove both endpoints of the complete declared integer domain fit I64 using
+checked I128 arithmetic. A small observed data range cannot admit I64 * 3.
+
+Do not admit casts, division, remainder, functions, lazy branches, floating
+expressions, computed group keys, unused projections, other reductions or
+explicit spill. They keep ordinary native execution. Preserve null propagation,
+first-occurrence group order, aliases and exact result schema, complete producer
+and generation checks, cancellation and resource denial. The existing spill
+selection runs first. No source replay or automatic strategy switch follows
+allocation failure.
+
+The admitted expression cannot fail on valid values. Prepare its original
+column and identity keys in projection order, then use the ordinary grouping
+owner. Compute each selected integer once and update every requested state.
+Each state sees the same row sequence and existing compensated integer-input
+SUM/AVG behavior; do not replace that behavior with weighted or reordered sums.
+No output is delivered before the complete producer succeeds. Charge temporary
+owners and retained group state through the current native context.
+
+## Frozen finite comparison
+
+One identical ignored Rust harness calls the real prepared relational API in
+both builds. Freeze source closure, features, Rust 1.99.0, release profile,
+harness and executable identities. Generate each immutable native file once,
+outside measured preparation, with the existing sequential native flat writer,
+65,536 rows per chunk, no file statistics and no external engine. Store complete
+input witnesses and file hashes. Each operation opens/binds its file afresh;
+preparation and returned engine execution clocks stay separate. Record their sum
+for the first-execution control, serialization, resource observations and cleanup.
+Host/cache state is uncontrolled and prehashing is explicit; this is not a
+storage-cold experiment.
+
+| Case | Rows / key domain | Purpose |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| dictionary_dense | 262,144 / 64 | Dictionary UTF8, 60% predicate selection; target |
+| dictionary_skew | 262,144 / 64 | Nine of ten non-null keys use key zero; target |
+| dictionary_sparse | 262,144 / 64 | Dictionary UTF8, 3% selection; target |
+| plain_high_cardinality | 65,536 / 8,192 | Plain UTF8, many retained groups; control |
+| tiny | 17 / 7 | Dictionary UTF8 and setup-sensitive execution; control |
+| ineligible_i64 | 65,536 / 64 | I64 input multiplication cannot pass the domain proof; control |
+
+All keys use non-ASCII text, with a null key every 97th row. The nullable
+integer is `(row % 1009) - 504`, null every 19th row; it is I32 except the
+ineligible I64 control. The I64 predicate value is `row % 5`, or `row % 100`
+for the sparse target. Select values from 1 through 3 inclusive, project the

+# Exact join counts without expanded row pairs
+
+Status: dropped at the maintainer's request after the combined Full43 checkpoint.
+The whole unmerged item-15 runtime batch is removed. The finite comparison below
+remains historical evidence; it does not describe the current runtime. See the
+[drop and restoration record](../benchmarks/native-workflow-drop-2026-10-25.md).
+This was the first mechanism in item 15's
+[workflow work-elimination package](native-workflow-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md).
+The baseline is merged #1605, `167ac248ba662ae7967a7801995e9b160b17bae5`.
+RFC 0044 and RFCs 0013–0017/0021–0022 govern the native plan, resource, semantic,
+streaming and error boundaries; no new phase or competitive-gate closure follows.
+
+## Existing component and extension
+
+The current prepared dispatcher is
+`local_primitive_prepared_relational.rs::PreparedVortexRelational::run`.
+An aggregate executes its input, and an ordinary inner join builds the right
+side, probes left rows, constructs bounded matching-pair arrays and gathers
+their output columns. Scalar `COUNT(*)` then adds those arrays' lengths.
+The handoff's two standalone join/aggregate dispatcher filenames do not exist;
+the current bound nodes and aggregate specification live in
+`local_primitive_relational_bind.rs` and
+`local_primitive_relational_aggregate_bind.rs`.
+
+Extend the existing exact `RowSet`/`RowIndex` and native `Batch` key owners with
+credited key multiplicities. Retain one native representative per non-null
+right key and a checked count, then probe every left key and add its matching
+multiplicity. This computes the same sum of left/right multiplicity products
+without retaining a second left table or enumerating matching row pairs.
+Use the existing scalar aggregate state and finalization for all requested
+COUNT aliases. Execution state stays local to each operation; repeated prepared
+calls recompute it.
+
+The existing RowSet equality, collision handling, first-occurrence order,
+gathering and backing ownership are the reuse boundary. Do not add a second
+key hash/equality implementation, factorized plan IR, cache, thread pool or
+external executor. Keep original children and right-before-left execution order.
+Complete both producers even when one side has no matching keys.
+
+When an entire input batch contributes new non-null keys, keep those native key
+arrays and their already prepared key owners directly. Remove unselected payload
+columns and retain the complete backing credits. Mixed/duplicate batches use the
+existing compact native gathering. Ordinary set/grouping consumers keep their
+existing retention path; this specialization belongs only to counted membership.
+
+Vortex-first check: pinned Vortex 0.90.0 supplies native arrays, builtins,
+validity, execution contexts and allocation owners used by the existing key
+and gather providers. The inspected `vortex-compute` crate exposes lane-level
+map kernels, not this relational join/aggregate consumer contract. This change
+extends ShardLoom's existing native relational algorithm around admitted Vortex
+owners (`wrap_existing_provider`); it adds no dependency or query-engine
+integration. Dictionary identity, native typed equality and complete backing
+charges stay with the existing providers.
+
+## Admission and semantic contract
+
+Admit only a scalar aggregate containing one or more `COUNT(*)` measures directly
+over an inner equality join with at least one key and no residual condition.
+All existing admitted key types must use their current exact key semantics.
+Composite keys with any SQL-null component do not match. Preserve empty-input
+zero, duplicate multiplicity, output U64/schema/aliases, checked count overflow,
+full producer/source-generation validation, cancellation and release on failure.
+No result is emitted before both complete inputs are accepted.
+
+The initial strategy does not replace the explicitly selected spill executor.
+Explicit-spill requests, outer/cross/semi/anti joins, residual conditions,
+grouped aggregates, COUNT(column), DISTINCT and other reductions keep their
+existing native strategies. A resident reservation failure remains a deterministic
+resource error; it must not replay a consumed source or silently switch strategy.
+Pressure validation must prove both that denial releases the counted state and
+that explicitly requested ordinary native spill still completes correctly.
+
+Keep public SQL, typed/DataFrame and native declarations on the same bound
+consumer path. Record actual activation, input rows, distinct retained right
+keys and represented matching pairs. Separate those facts from materialized
+join rows. Preserve source/error work even when output payload is unused.
+
+The completed report exposes `counted_join_stages`, `counted_join_build_rows`,
+`counted_join_probe_rows`, `counted_join_distinct_build_keys` and
+`counted_join_represented_pairs`; public route fields add the existing
+`relational_` prefix. Counters sum actual completed stages. Represented pairs
+are cardinality contributions, not materialized output rows or a speed claim.
+
+## Frozen comparison
+
+Use one identical test harness through the real prepared relational API in
+baseline and candidate release builds, with the same Rust toolchain, features,
+ThinLTO profile and source data. Freeze harness, executables, source and expected
+result hashes before each comparison. Setup includes source registration and
+binding; engine time comes from the returned execution clock. Record both,
+plus serialization, memory and cleanup. Ordinary host/cache state is uncontrolled;
+do not label the comparison storage-cold or attribute unrelated host activity.
+
+| Case | Left/right rows | Key domain and purpose |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| Duplicate numeric target | 8,192 / 16,384 | 64 numeric keys; 2,097,152 matching pairs |
+| Composite text target | 4,096 / 8,192 | 32 UTF8-plus-integer keys with non-ASCII text; 1,048,576 pairs |
+| Skew target | 1,024 / 2,048 | Nine of each ten positions share one key; other positions have unique keys |
+| Unique-match control | 32,768 / 32,768 | One matching right row per left key |
+| Unique-no-match control | 32,768 / 32,768 | Disjoint exact key ranges |
+| Tiny control | 17 / 23 | Seven numeric keys; setup-sensitive complete operation |
+| Ineligible aggregate control | 8,192 / 8,192 | Unique keys with COUNT(column), keeping the ordinary path |
+
+All cases use a single existing CPU allocation and a 128-MiB native grant.
+Generate immutable input values outside measured preparation. Independently
+derive the complete scalar answer and authoritative schema from those values;
+do not use another execution strategy's result as the sole oracle. Include
+streamed/schema-only source variants in correctness proof, and keep prospective
+comparison inputs fixed across both roles.
+
+Run two complete cohorts with three paired samples per case. Alternate
+baseline/candidate order within the first cohort and reverse it in the second.
+No sample is silently retried, replaced or removed. Each target must improve
+median complete-workload engine time by at least 2% in both cohorts. Every
+case's median engine time and preparation-plus-engine time must remain within
+5% of its control; the tiny case also allows an absolute 50-microsecond increase
+to avoid deciding from timer-scale noise. This absolute allowance applies only
+to the predeclared tiny control. Resource ownership and complete result gates
+must pass regardless of timing.
+
+Run separate debug-observation executions to establish zero matching-pair
+construction in admitted candidates, exact represented cardinality, complete
+input consumption and unique-key retention. Do not mix instrumented times into
+the release score. Preserve every failure and partial cohort. A failed gate is
+a revise/drop decision, not permission to add repetitions until a favorable
+result appears. A materially different revision requires a new explicit protocol;
+the original failed decision remains visible.
+
+## Correctness and completion
+
+Test mixed/all-null and empty keys, composite strings and integers, dictionary
+identity and slicing, duplicates across batches, forced hash collisions, skew,
+checked count overflow without constructing impossible-sized inputs, and every
+non-admission boundary. Exercise source changes, late producer errors, schema
+drift, cancellation, denied reservations and complete resource release. Verify
+write/readback and equivalent SQL/DataFrame declarations at package acceptance.
+
+Run focused native unit/integration checks before the required workspace
+format/lint/tests, native suite and public/installed-package acceptance for the
+cohesive package. Retained runtime changes receive one isolated standard Full43
+pass at that boundary, exactly one call per independent query. Do not use Full43
+to replace the composed-workflow proof, reduce its correctness checks, or claim
+that a join-count benefit is a whole-engine speedup. The following fused pipeline
+and remaining item-15 packages keep their own acceptance decisions.
+
+## October 25 mechanism decision
+
+The initial finite decision was to retain the candidate; the subsequent whole-item

+The three duplicate-heavy targets reduce engine time by 97.2–99.5% across the

+
+Fourteen separate debug executions verify the mechanism. Eligible candidates

+The final native suite passes 3,312 tests with 33 intentionally ignored cost

+The [compact evidence manifest](../benchmarks/evidence/native-join-count-2026-10-25/manifest.json)

+recomputes complete answers, source-delivery and mechanism counters, and both

+
+Workspace, public SQL/DataFrame, writer/readback, installed-package and the

+The next implementation mechanism is the composed encoded scan-to-aggregate

+# One computation for an explicit multi-output request
+
+Status: dropped with the entire item-15 batch at the maintainer's request.
+The implementation is removed; public/installed-package and finite multi-output
+performance acceptance were not completed. The following is the historical
+candidate contract, preserved with its tests and failures in the
+[drop record](../benchmarks/native-workflow-drop-2026-10-25.md).
+This extends package 1 in the
+[workflow handoff](native-workflow-work-elimination-2026-10-25.md) after the
+counted-join and computed-measure finite decisions. RFC 0044, RFC 0033 and
+RFCs 0013–0017 retain execution, resource, correctness and publication ownership.
+
+## Existing boundary and chosen extension
+
+`PreparedVortexRelational::write_many_controlled` currently invokes the ordinary
+writer for each destination. Retained sources and the budget are shared, but
+computation repeats. The existing `write_many_with_input` path already computes
+a batch-input plan once and stages all outputs from a credited native result.
+Promote that owner to retained file and memory sources with an optional input
+provider. One destination keeps direct streaming. Multiple destinations use
+the existing native replay recorder and independent output adapters.
+
+Pinned Vortex 0.90.0 supplies native arrays, allocation owners, file streams and
+writers. ShardLoom's existing native result, replay and publication boundaries
+already coordinate these providers. This is `use_vortex_native_provider` through
+the existing local-primitives/write feature gates and execution/I/O certificates.
+There is no new executor, output representation, dependency, global answer cache
+or worker pool. Vortex remains native; compatibility writers retain their
+existing fidelity/type limits and `fallback_attempted=false`.
+
+The native primitive routes are part of the same completion unit. Their existing
+count, unary, aggregate, sort, partitioned and relational providers must produce
+once through native bounded delivery. Do not route them through the small owned
+collector, which has independent row/byte limits and spill exclusions. Preserve
+provider selection and complete source/generation validation. The existing batch
+input path must continue to consume every declared producer exactly once.
+
+## Ownership, failure and compatibility
+
+Admit targets and adapters before demanding input. A complete native result is
+retained under the original grant; without spill permission, exceeding that grant
+is an explicit resource refusal. With explicit spill, replay uses native runs,
+the declared disk quota and owned cleanup. No source replay or strategy retry may
+follow a failed reservation. This retention requirement is now explicit for
+repeatable sources too; single-output streaming remains available without it.
+The relational policy owns one run store across producing operators and output
+replay. Existing primitive aggregate/sort spill declarations admit only their
+operator. Their output replay remains resident under the same grant; do not
+duplicate an operator's disk quota into an independent replay allowance. A
+shared primitive disk-quota extension requires separate owner work. This
+distinction must appear in pressure tests and public limitations.
+
+Every producer must finish and every adapter must complete privately before
+publication. Release replay owners and finish native cleanup before certifying
+success. Revalidate all source generations and targets before publishing. A late
+publication failure preserves already published complete outputs and identifies
+them for recovery; independent files do not become an atomic group. Preserve
+foreign files and existing destinations on failure. Sampling preparation begins
+once per request and remains provisional until publication succeeds.
+
+Use the existing `WrittenVortexRelationalFanout` result: one execution certificate,
+an ordered output list and optional replay observations. Coordinate the internal
+Rust `write_many`/`write_many_controlled` return-type change and their callers;
+the old vector of per-destination execution reports cannot describe this contract
+without duplicating credited metadata. These workspace Rust crates are not
+published APIs. Python/CLI method names, arguments, output order and per-target
+publication fields remain stable. Existing execution-count and strategy fields
+must report one computation and the actual replay mode. No second public method
+is introduced for an alternative implementation.
+
+## Required proof
+
+Check complete ordered readback and exact schemas for all eight existing writers,
+file and memory sources, typed empties, nulls, duplicates, composed joins and
+aggregates, dynamic schemas and independent repeated requests. Prove exactly one
+execution per successful multi-output request; a later independent request must
+compute again. Cover single-output control, preflight refusal before demand,
+late producer/schema/generation errors, later-adapter failure, cancellation,
+publication failure, sampling-model invalidation, reservation denial and explicit
+native spill. Returned reports and abandoned/failed calls must release credits.
+
+The finite comparison must include an expensive composed computation with
+multiple outputs, a cheap/count control, a single-output control and output that
+exceeds the small collector's limits. Freeze its source/inputs, complete native
+write boundary, separate query/output observations, paired schedule and target/
+control gates before any comparison call. A lower execution counter alone is
+not a whole-workflow timing claim. Preserve every result, failure and refusal.
+
+Final acceptance also requires the public SQL/DataFrame and installed-package
+routes, the required native/default checks, portable evidence, and the coherent
+package's isolated Full43 before PR integration. Explicit shared branches and
+guarded decorrelation follow under their own semantic admission contracts.
+
+## Existing single-output resource limit
+
+The retained-file pressure fixture has 65,537 strings of 256 bytes in separate
+251-row native leaves. Relational single-output streaming completes under its
+16 MiB grant, while both existing primitive direct Vortex and Parquet writers
+refuse reservations under that grant. The primitive projection's singleton
+dispatch, scan and output implementations are unchanged by this fanout work.
+Its pressure test therefore proves refusal without reexecution, publication or
+leaked owners; it does not claim that all singleton providers fit this grant.

+"""Retire exact completed experiment payloads after independent portable proof."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import stat
+import subprocess
+
+P = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+E = Path('/Users/dylan/.codex/worktrees/public-docs-api/shardloom-local-repo/docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-fused-measure-2026-10-25')
+RETAINED = Path('/Users/dylan/LocalData/shardloom/ingest-ownership-20261025/combined-runtime-r1')
+
+
+def digest(path):
+    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def generation(path):
+    info = path.lstat()
+    assert stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and not path.is_symlink(), str(path)
+    return info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns
+
+
+def main():
+    destination = E / 'cleanup.json'
+    assert not destination.exists()
+    manifest = json.loads((E / 'manifest.json').read_text())
+    validation = json.loads((E / 'portable-validation.json').read_text())
+    packet_sha = digest(E / 'packet.tar.gz')
+    assert packet_sha == manifest['archive']['sha256'] == validation['packet_sha256']
+    assert validation['verifier_sha256'] == digest(E / 'verify.py')
+    assert validation['status'] == 'passed' and validation['engine_executions'] == 0
+    result = validation['portable_result']
+    assert result['portable_replay_passed']
+    assert result['comparison']['all_timing_gates_passed']
+    assert result['observations']['work_elimination_observations_passed']
+    assert RETAINED.is_dir() and not RETAINED.is_symlink()
+    archived = {entry['path']: entry for entry in manifest['files']}
+    expected = []
+
+    def saved_json(relative):
+        source = P / relative
+        assert digest(source) == archived[relative]['sha256']
+        return json.loads(source.read_text())
+
+    variants = {
+        ('r1', 'baseline'): ('release', 'observe'),
+        ('r1', 'candidate'): ('release', 'observe'),
+        ('r2', 'baseline'): ('release', 'observe'),
+        ('r2', 'candidate'): ('observe',),
+        ('r3', 'candidate'): ('release', 'observe'),
+    }
+    for (revision, role), labels in variants.items():
+        for label in labels:
+            prefix = f'fused-measure-{role}-runtime-{revision}'
+            runtime = saved_json(f'{prefix}/{label}-manifest.json')
+            path = P / prefix / f'shardloom-fused-measure-{label}'
+            assert path == Path(runtime['binary'])
+            expected.append((path, runtime['binary_sha256'], None, 'comparison_executable'))
+    json_repro = saved_json('fused-measure-json-repro-identity-r1.json')['identities']['binary']
+    expected.append((P / 'fused-measure-json-repro-r1', json_repro['sha256'],
+                     json_repro['bytes'], 'diagnostic_executable'))
+    encoding = saved_json('fused-measure-encoding-repro-identity-r1.json')['identities']
+    for revision in ('r1', 'r2'):
+        name = f'fused-measure-encoding-repro-{revision}'
+        expected.append((P / name, encoding[name]['sha256'], encoding[name]['bytes'],
+                         'diagnostic_executable'))
+    inputs = saved_json('fused-measure-inputs-r1/manifest.json')
+    for case, identity in inputs.items():
+        expected.append((P / 'fused-measure-inputs-r1' / f'{case}.vortex',
+                         identity['sha256'], identity['bytes'], 'finite_native_fixture'))
+    assert len(expected) == 18 and len({path for path, *_ in expected}) == 18
+    records = []
+    generations = {}
+    for path, identity, size, kind in expected:
+        assert path.is_relative_to(P) and path.resolve() == path
+        assert not path.is_relative_to(RETAINED)
+        before = generation(path)
+        assert digest(path) == identity and generation(path) == before
+        assert size is None or before[2] == size
+        generations[path] = before
+        records.append({'path': str(path), 'sha256': identity, 'bytes': before[2],
+                        'kind': kind, 'open_handles': False})
+    handles = subprocess.run(['/usr/sbin/lsof', '-t', '--',
+                              *(str(path) for path, *_ in expected)],
+                             text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
+    assert handles.returncode == 1 and not handles.stdout.strip() and not handles.stderr.strip(), handles
+    assert all(generation(path) == before for path, before in generations.items())
+    retired = []
+    report = {'status': 'running', 'retired_files': retired, 'packet_sha256': packet_sha,
+              'driver_sha256': digest(Path(__file__)),
+              'basis': 'completed finite comparison; independently replayed packet retains complete values, failures, clocks, native input witnesses, source overlays and regeneration harness',
+              'accepted_runtime_preserved': str(RETAINED),
+              'compiler_cache_retained_for_active_work': True,
+              'accepted_benchmark_source_inputs_preserved': True, 'backups_created': False}
+    try:
+        for item in records:
+            path = Path(item['path'])
+            assert generation(path) == generations[path]
+            path.unlink()
+            retired.append(item)
+        assert all(not Path(item['path']).exists() for item in retired)
+        report['status'] = 'passed'
+    finally:
+        report['retired_bytes'] = sum(item['bytes'] for item in retired)
+        with destination.open('x') as stream:
+            json.dump(report, stream, indent=2)
+            stream.write('\n')
+    print(json.dumps({'status': report['status'], 'retired_files': len(retired),
+                      'retired_bytes': report['retired_bytes']}))
+
+

+"""Check isolated replay and reject corruption without starting the engine."""
+import copy
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+P = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+W = Path('/Users/dylan/.codex/worktrees/public-docs-api/shardloom-local-repo')
+E = W / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-fused-measure-2026-10-25'
+
+
+def sha(raw):
+    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+
+
+def main():
+    report_path = P / 'fused-measure-portable-validation-r3.json'
+    assert not report_path.exists()
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('fused_packet_verifier', E / 'verify.py')
+    v = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(v)
+    verifier_sha = sha((E / 'verify.py').read_bytes())
+    packet = v.Packet(E)
+    checks = []
+
+    def rejects(name, function):
+        try:
+            function()
+        except (AssertionError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError, FileNotFoundError) as error:
+            checks.append({'name': name, 'outcome': 'rejected',
+                           'diagnostic': type(error).__name__ + ': ' + str(error)})
+        else:
+            raise AssertionError('corruption accepted: ' + name)
+
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fused-measure-portable-r3-', dir=P / 'tmp') as temporary:
+        directory = Path(temporary)
+        for name in ('verify.py', 'manifest.json', 'packet.tar.gz'):
+            shutil.copy2(E / name, directory / name)
+        active = True
+        forbidden = []
+
+        def audit(event, args):
+            if not active or event != 'open' or not isinstance(args[0], (str, bytes)):
+                return
+            path = str(Path(args[0]).absolute())
+            if path.startswith((str(P) + '/', str(W) + '/')) and not path.startswith(str(directory) + '/'):
+                forbidden.append(path)
+                raise ValueError('original file access during isolated replay')
+
+        sys.addaudithook(audit)
+        result = v.verify(directory)
+        active = False
+        assert result['portable_replay_passed'] and not forbidden
+        checks.append({'name': 'isolated_copy_with_original_reads_denied', 'outcome': 'passed'})
+        manifest_bytes = (directory / 'manifest.json').read_bytes()
+        manifest = json.loads(manifest_bytes)
+        lost = manifest['files'].pop()
+        manifest['raw_member_bytes'] -= lost['bytes']
+        (directory / 'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
+        rejects('missing_archive_member', lambda: v.Packet(directory))
+        manifest = json.loads(manifest_bytes)
+        manifest['files'][0]['path'] = '../outside'
+        (directory / 'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
+        rejects('archive_path_traversal', lambda: v.Packet(directory))
+        (directory / 'manifest.json').write_bytes(manifest_bytes)
+        raw = bytearray((directory / 'packet.tar.gz').read_bytes())
+        raw[-20] ^= 1
+        (directory / 'packet.tar.gz').write_bytes(raw)
+        rejects('corrupt_archive_bytes', lambda: v.Packet(directory))
+
+    def edited_packet(name, edit):
+        changed = copy.copy(packet)
+        changed.files = packet.files.copy()
+        value = json.loads(changed.files[name])
+        edit(value)
+        changed.files[name] = json.dumps(value).encode()
+        return changed
+
+    missing = edited_packet('fused-measure-comparison-r3/outcome.json', lambda x: x['calls'].pop())
+    rejects('missing_timing_call', lambda: v.verify_cohort(missing, 'measure'))
+    original_missing = edited_packet('fused-measure-observations-r1/outcome.json', lambda x: x['calls'].clear())
+    rejects('missing_failed_first_attempt', lambda: v.verify_first_attempt(original_missing))
+    changed = edited_packet('fused-measure-observations-r3/protocol.json',
+                            lambda x: x['frozen_protocol'].__setitem__('text', 'altered'))
+    rejects('changed_frozen_protocol', lambda: v.verify_cohort(changed, 'observe'))
+
+    missing_activation = edited_packet('fused-measure-observations-r2/outcome.json', lambda x: x['calls'].pop())
+    rejects('missing_failed_activation_call', lambda: v.verify_cohort(missing_activation, 'observe', 'r2'))
+    claimed_activation = edited_packet('fused-measure-failed-observe-verification-r2.json',
+        lambda x: x.__setitem__('work_elimination_observations_passed', True))
+    rejects('failed_activation_relabelled_as_success', lambda: v.verify_cohort(claimed_activation, 'observe', 'r2'))
+
+    root = 'fused-measure-observations-r3'
+    normal = packet.read(root + '/observe-dictionary_dense-candidate-0-0.json')
+
+    def witness(identity):
+        return packet.read(root + '/witnesses/' + identity + '.json')
+
+    v.values(normal, witness)
+    for label, field, edit in (
+        ('wrong_ordered_result', 'actual_rows_witness', lambda x: x.reverse()),
+        ('wrong_sum', 'actual_rows_witness', lambda x: x[0].__setitem__('sum', 1.0)),
+        ('wrong_count_type', 'actual_rows_witness', lambda x: x[0].__setitem__('rows', True)),
+        ('wrong_schema', 'schema_witness', lambda x: x['Struct'][0]['dtypes'][3]['Primitive'].__setitem__(1, False)),
+        ('wrong_complete_input', 'input_witness', lambda x: x['n'].__setitem__(1, 999)),
+    ):
+        value = witness(normal[field])
+        edit(value)
+        rejects(label, lambda: v.values(normal, lambda identity: value if identity == normal[field] else witness(identity)))
+    rejects('wrong_original_json', lambda: v.values(normal, lambda identity:
+            '{}' if identity == normal['raw_rows_witness'] else witness(identity)))
+    for label, edit in (
+        ('missing_actual_dictionary_domains', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('variable_dictionary_domains', 0)),
+        ('wrong_source_rows', lambda x: x.__setitem__('native_io_certificate', x['native_io_certificate'].replace('delivered_scan_rows=' + str(x['selected_rows']), 'delivered_scan_rows=0'))),
+        ('extra_dictionary_domains', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('variable_dictionary_domains', 1 + x['observations']['variable_dictionary_domains'])),
+        ('missing_dictionary_values', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('variable_dictionary_domain_values', 0)),
+        ('intermediate_still_constructed', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('expression_rows_constructed', 1)),
+        ('wrong_mapped_rows', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('fused_measure_rows', 0)),
+        ('wrong_aggregate_updates', lambda x: x['observations'].__setitem__('aggregate_row_updates', 0)),
+        ('false_public_activation', lambda x: x.__setitem__('native_io_certificate', x['native_io_certificate'].replace('fused_measure_stages=1', 'fused_measure_stages=0'))),
+        ('owner_leak', lambda x: x.__setitem__('reserved_after_cleanup', 1)),
+        ('over_grant', lambda x: x.__setitem__('peak_reserved_bytes', 129 * v.MIB)),
+        ('fallback', lambda x: x.__setitem__('native_io_certificate', x['native_io_certificate'].replace('fallback_attempted: false', 'fallback_attempted: true'))),
+        ('extra_cpu', lambda x: x.__setitem__('runtime', x['runtime'].replace('admitted_max_parallelism: 1', 'admitted_max_parallelism: 2'))),
+        ('missing_clock', lambda x: x.pop('engine_execution_ns')),
+    ):
+        record = copy.deepcopy(normal)
+        edit(record)
+        rejects(label, lambda: v.values(record, witness))
+    observed, observation = v.verify_cohort(packet, 'observe')
+    measured, measurement = v.verify_cohort(packet, 'measure')
+    original = v.verify_first_attempt(packet)
+    _, failed_observation = v.verify_cohort(packet, 'observe', 'r2')
+    changed = edited_packet('fused-measure-source-candidate-r2.json',
+                            lambda x: x['after_source_inventory'].__setitem__('Cargo.toml', '0' * 64))
+    rejects('production_change_hidden_as_harness_fix',
+            lambda: v.verify_harness_repair(changed, original, failed_observation))
+    hidden_runtime = copy.deepcopy(observation)
+    hidden_runtime['runtime_manifests']['candidate']['source_inventory']['Cargo.toml'] = '0' * 64
+    rejects('encoding_fix_changes_unrelated_runtime', lambda: v.verify_encoding_correction(packet, failed_observation, hidden_runtime))
+    changed_baseline = copy.deepcopy(observation)
+    changed_baseline['runtime_manifests']['baseline']['binary_sha256'] = '0' * 64
+    rejects('reused_baseline_identity_changed', lambda: v.verify_encoding_correction(packet, failed_observation, changed_baseline))
+    missing_source = copy.copy(packet)
+    missing_source.files = packet.files.copy()
+    del missing_source.files['fused-measure-failed-tests-source-r3.tar.gz']
+    rejects('failed_test_source_missing', lambda: v.verify_encoding_correction(missing_source, failed_observation, observation))
+    records = {}
+    for case, role, cohort, sample in v.schedule('measure'):
+        records[(case, role, cohort, sample)] = packet.read(
+            f'fused-measure-comparison-r3/measure-{case}-{role}-{cohort}-{sample}.json')
+    assert v.score(records) == {key: measured[key] for key in ('all_timing_gates_passed', 'cells')}
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(records)
+    for sample in (1, 2, 3):
+        changed[('dictionary_sparse', 'candidate', 2, sample)]['engine_execution_ns'] *= 1000
+    changed_score = v.score(changed)
+    assert not changed_score['all_timing_gates_passed'] and changed_score != v.score(records)
+    checks.append({'name': 'second_cohort_regression_changes_frozen_decision', 'outcome': 'passed'})
+    result = {'status': 'passed', 'engine_executions': 0, 'checks': checks,
+        'verifier_sha256': verifier_sha, 'validator_sha256': sha(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
+        'packet_sha256': packet.manifest['archive']['sha256'], 'portable_result': result,
+        'temporary_fixtures_retired': True}
+    with report_path.open('x') as stream:
+        json.dump(result, stream, indent=2)
+        stream.write('\n')
+    print(json.dumps({'status': 'passed', 'checks': len(checks), 'engine_executions': 0}))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':

+def digest(raw):
+    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+
+
+def strict(raw):
+    def unique(pairs):
+        result = {}
+        for key, value in pairs:
+            assert key not in result, 'duplicate JSON key'
+            result[key] = value
+        return result
+
+    def finite(value):
+        number = float(value)
+        assert math.isfinite(number), 'nonfinite JSON number'
+        return number
+
+    def invalid(value):
+        raise ValueError('nonfinite JSON constant: ' + value)
+
+    return json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_float=finite, parse_constant=invalid)
+

+def safe(name):
+    return (isinstance(name, str) and bool(name) and not name.startswith('/')
+            and all(part not in ('', '.', '..') for part in name.split('/'))
+            and str(PurePosixPath(name)) == name)
+

+class Packet:
+    def __init__(self, directory):
+        self.manifest = strict((directory / 'manifest.json').read_bytes())
+        manifest = self.manifest
+        assert manifest['schema_version'] == 'shardloom.native_fused_measure.packet.v3'
+        assert manifest['baseline_head'] == HEAD
+        assert manifest['status'] == 'finite_mechanism_evidence_captured_package_acceptance_pending'
+        expected = {}
+        for identity in manifest['files']:
+            name = identity['path']
+            assert safe(name) and name not in expected
+            assert type(identity['bytes']) is int and 0 <= identity['bytes'] <= 64 * MIB
+            assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', identity['sha256'])
+            expected[name] = identity
+        assert sum(item['bytes'] for item in expected.values()) == manifest['raw_member_bytes']
+        assert manifest['raw_member_bytes'] <= 64 * MIB
+        archive = manifest['archive']
+        assert archive['path'] == 'packet.tar.gz' and 0 < archive['bytes'] <= 64 * MIB
+        path = directory / archive['path']
+        assert not path.is_symlink() and path.stat().st_size == archive['bytes']
+        raw = path.read_bytes()
+        assert digest(raw) == archive['sha256']
+        self.files = {}
+        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw), mode='r:gz') as stream:
+            for entry in stream:
+                assert safe(entry.name) and entry.name in expected and entry.name not in self.files
+                identity = expected[entry.name]
+                assert entry.isfile() and entry.size == identity['bytes']
+                data = stream.extractfile(entry).read()
+                assert len(data) == identity['bytes'] and digest(data) == identity['sha256']
+                self.files[entry.name] = data
+        assert self.files.keys() == expected.keys(), 'missing archive member'
+        assert {name for name in self.files if not name.startswith((
+            'fused-measure-comparison-r3/', 'fused-measure-observations-r3/',

+def independent_input(case):
+    rows, keys = CASES[case]
+    return {'domain': [f'clé-東京-{key}' for key in range(keys)] + [None],
+            'codes': [keys if row % 97 == 0 else
+                      0 if case == 'dictionary_skew' and row % 10 != 9 else row % keys
+                      for row in range(rows)],
+            'n': [None if row % 19 == 0 else (row % 1009) - 504 for row in range(rows)],
+            'p': [row % (100 if case == 'dictionary_sparse' else 5) for row in range(rows)]}
+

+def oracle(data):
+    groups = {}
+    selected = 0
+    for code, number, predicate in zip(data['codes'], data['n'], data['p'], strict=True):
+        if predicate < 1 or predicate > 3:
+            continue
+        selected += 1
+        group = groups.setdefault(data['domain'][code], [0, 0, 0])
+        group[0] += 1
+        if number is not None:
+            group[1] += 1
+            group[2] += number * 3
+    result = []
+    for key, (rows, count, total) in groups.items():
+        assert abs(total) < 2**53 and count < 2**53
+        result.append({'group': key, 'rows': rows, 'values': count,
+                       'sum': float(total) if count else None,
+                       'avg': total / count if count else None})
+    return result, selected

+def number(text, name):
+    found = re.findall(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r':\s*(\d+)\b', text)
+    assert len(found) == 1, name
+    return int(found[0])

+def values(record, witness, revision='r3'):
+    case = record['case']
+    data = witness(record['input_witness'])
+    assert data == independent_input(case), 'frozen input: ' + case
+    expected, selected = oracle(data)
+    assert record['input_rows'] == CASES[case][0] and record['selected_rows'] == selected
+    assert witness(record['schema_witness']) == SCHEMA
+    assert record['expected_rows_witness'] == record['actual_rows_witness']
+    actual = witness(record['actual_rows_witness'])
+    assert actual == expected, 'full ordered values: ' + case
+    raw = witness(record['raw_rows_witness'])
+    assert isinstance(raw, str)
+    assert [strict(line) for line in raw.splitlines()] == expected, 'raw emitted JSON'
+    for row in actual:
+        assert set(row) == {'group', 'rows', 'values', 'sum', 'avg'}
+        assert type(row['rows']) is int and type(row['values']) is int
+        assert row['sum'] is None or type(row['sum']) is float
+        assert row['avg'] is None or type(row['avg']) is float
+    for name in ('engine_execution_ns', 'preparation_ns', 'result_serialization_ns'):
+        assert type(record[name]) is int and record[name] >= 0
+    assert record['engine_execution_ns'] > 0
+    assert record['complete_values_match'] is True and record['complete_schema_match'] is True
+    assert record['memory_grant_bytes'] == 128 * MIB
+    assert type(record['peak_reserved_bytes']) is int
+    assert 0 <= record['peak_reserved_bytes'] <= record['memory_grant_bytes']
+    assert record['denied_reservations'] == record['reserved_after_cleanup'] == 0
+    certificate = record['native_io_certificate']
+    assert 'schema_version: "shardloom.native_io_certificate.v1"' in certificate
+    assert 'diagnostics: []' in certificate
+    fallback = re.findall(r'\bfallback_attempted:\s*(true|false)', certificate)
+    assert fallback and set(fallback) == {'false'} and 'fallback_execution_allowed: false' in certificate
+    for name, expected_value in [('completed_executions', 1), ('admitted_max_parallelism', 1),
+                                 ('provider_background_workers', 0), ('limit_bytes', 128 * MIB),
+                                 ('denied_reservations', 0)]:
+        assert number(record['runtime'], name) == expected_value, name
+    active = record['role'] == 'candidate' and case != 'ineligible_i64'
+    if record['role'] == 'candidate':
+        for name, value in [('fused_measure_stages', int(active)),
+                            ('fused_measure_rows', selected if active else 0)]:
+            found = re.findall(r'\b' + name + r'=(\d+)\b', certificate)
+            assert found == [str(value)], (case, name, found)
+    delivered = re.findall(r'\bdelivered_scan_rows=(\d+)\b', certificate)
+    batches = re.findall(r'\bnative_batches=(\d+)\b', certificate)
+    assert delivered == [str(selected)] and len(batches) == 1 and int(batches[0]) > 0
+    if record['observation_enabled']:
+        counts = record['observations']
+        assert isinstance(counts, dict) and all(type(value) is int and value >= 0 for value in counts.values())
+        assert counts['fused_measure_stages'] == int(active)
+        assert counts['fused_measure_rows'] == (selected if active else 0)
+        assert counts['expression_rows_constructed'] == (0 if active else selected)
+        assert counts['aggregate_row_updates'] == selected * 4
+        assert counts['variable_domains'] > 0
+        assert revision in ('r2', 'r3')
+        encoded = revision == 'r3' and active and case != 'plain_high_cardinality'
+        domains = int(batches[0]) if encoded else 0
+        entries = domains * (CASES[case][1] + 1)
+        if record['role'] == 'candidate':
+            assert counts['variable_dictionary_domains'] == domains
+            assert counts['variable_dictionary_domain_values'] == entries
+        assert counts['variable_domain_values'] == (entries if encoded else selected) + len(expected)
+    else:
+        assert record['observations'] is None

+def score(records):
+    results, passed = {}, True
+    for cohort in (1, 2):
+        for case in CASES:
+            medians = {}
+            for role in ('baseline', 'candidate'):
+                runs = [records[(case, role, cohort, sample)] for sample in (1, 2, 3)]
+                medians[role] = {'engine_ns': statistics.median(row['engine_execution_ns'] for row in runs),
+                    'preparation_engine_ns': statistics.median(row['engine_execution_ns'] + row['preparation_ns'] for row in runs)}
+            allowance = 50000 if case == 'tiny' else 0
+            control = all(medians['candidate'][clock] <= max(medians['baseline'][clock] * 1.05,
+                medians['baseline'][clock] + allowance) for clock in ('engine_ns', 'preparation_engine_ns'))
+            target = case not in TARGETS or medians['candidate']['engine_ns'] <= medians['baseline']['engine_ns'] * .98
+            passed &= control and target
+            results[f'{cohort}:{case}'] = {'medians': medians, 'control_passed': control, 'target_passed': target}
+    return {'all_timing_gates_passed': passed, 'cells': results}

+def checked_receipt(packet, name, passed=True):
+    receipt, raw = packet.read(name + '.json'), packet.raw(name + '.log')
+    assert receipt['head'] == HEAD and digest(raw) == receipt['log_sha256']
+    assert receipt['status'] == ('passed' if passed else 'failed')
+    assert (receipt['returncode'] == 0) is passed
+    assert receipt['direct_child_reaped'] and receipt['process_group_drained']
+    assert not receipt['timed_out'] and receipt['interrupted_signal'] is None
+    return receipt, raw.decode()

+def checked_manifest(packet, manifest, role, mode, revision='r2'):
+    assert revision in ('r1', 'r2', 'r3')
+    harness_sha = OLD_HARNESS_SHA if revision == 'r1' else HARNESS_SHA
+    directory = f'fused-measure-{role}-runtime-{revision}'
+    label = 'release' if mode == 'measure' else 'observe'
+    assert packet.read(f'{directory}/{label}-manifest.json') == manifest
+    assert manifest['revision'] == HEAD and manifest['features'] == ['release-user-surfaces']
+    assert manifest['profile'] == ('release' if mode == 'measure' else 'ci-native')
+    assert manifest['harnesses'] == {HARNESS: harness_sha}
+    assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', manifest['binary_sha256'])
+    assert manifest['binary'] == ORIGINAL + directory + '/shardloom-fused-measure-' + label
+    source = manifest['source_inventory']
+    assert len(source) == (2130 if role == 'baseline' else 2134) and source[HARNESS] == harness_sha
+    assert all(safe(name) and re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{64}', sha) for name, sha in source.items())
+    overlay = manifest['source_overlay']
+    members = {}
+    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(packet.linked(overlay)), mode='r:gz') as stream:
+        for entry in stream:
+            assert entry.isfile() and safe(entry.name) and entry.name not in members
+            assert entry.name in overlay['members'] and 0 <= entry.size <= 2 * MIB
+            raw = stream.extractfile(entry).read()
+            assert digest(raw) == overlay['members'][entry.name] == source[entry.name]
+            members[entry.name] = digest(raw)
+    assert members == overlay['members'] and len(members) == (18 if role == 'baseline' else 24)
+    receipt = strict(packet.linked(manifest['build_receipt']))
+    name = manifest['build_receipt']['path'][len(ORIGINAL):-5]

+    assert before[HARNESS] == after[HARNESS] == HARNESS_SHA
+    assert corrected['runtime_manifests']['baseline'] == failed['runtime_manifests']['baseline']
+    assert corrected['input_inventory_before'] == failed['input_inventory_before']
+    assert corrected['original_frozen_protocol'] == failed['frozen_protocol']

+    assert "assert counts['variable_dictionary_domains'] > 0" in log

+                                     ORIGINAL + 'fused-measure-observations-r2']
+
+    # The original broad suite belongs to the pre-encoding candidate, including
+    # its original harness. It cannot certify the later production correction.
+    prior_suite, log = checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-suite-r1')
+    assert '3322 passed; 0 failed; 35 ignored;' in log
+    for name, sha in failed['runtime_manifests']['candidate']['source_overlay']['members'].items():

+    assert validation['status'] == 'passed' and validation['engine_executions'] == 0

+def verify(directory):
+    packet = Packet(directory)
+    original = verify_first_attempt(packet)
+    observed, observation = verify_cohort(packet, 'observe')
+    measured, measurement = verify_cohort(packet, 'measure')
+    _, failed_observation = verify_cohort(packet, 'observe', 'r2')
+    verify_harness_repair(packet, original, failed_observation)
+    verify_encoding_correction(packet, failed_observation, observation)
+    for role in ('baseline', 'candidate'):
+        for key in ('source_inventory', 'harnesses', 'toolchain', 'features', 'revision'):
+            assert observation['runtime_manifests'][role][key] == measurement['runtime_manifests'][role][key]
+    assert observation['input_inventory_before'] == measurement['input_inventory_before']
+    assert observation['frozen_protocol'] == measurement['frozen_protocol']
+    candidate = measurement['runtime_manifests']['candidate']['source_overlay']['members']
+    suite, log = checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-suite-r3')
+    assert '3324 passed; 0 failed; 35 ignored;' in log
+    for name, sha in candidate.items():
+        assert suite['changed_source_inventory'][name]['sha256'] == sha
+    assert suite['command'] == [observation['runtime_manifests']['candidate']['binary'], '--test-threads=1']
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-focused-r1', False)
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-clippy-r1', False)
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-focused-r2')
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-clippy-r2')
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-clippy-r3')
+    checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-clippy-r4')
+    clippy, _ = checked_receipt(packet, 'fused-measure-native-clippy-r5')
+    for name, sha in candidate.items():
+        assert clippy['changed_source_inventory'][name]['sha256'] == sha
+    return {'portable_replay_passed': True, 'engine_executions': 0,
+            'failed_first_attempt_preserved': True, 'failed_dictionary_activation_preserved': True,
+            'production_source_unchanged_by_harness_repair': True,
+            'encoding_correction_limited_to_fused_consumer_and_regression': True,
+            'observations': observed, 'comparison': measured,
+            'package_acceptance': 'pending'}

+    def rejects(name, function, reason):

+            function()
+        except ValueError as error:

+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='join-count-portable-r1-', dir=P / 'tmp') as temporary:

+            shutil.copy2(E / name, directory / name)
+        active = True
+        forbidden_reads = []
+
+        def audit(event, args):
+            if not active or event != 'open' or not isinstance(args[0], (str, bytes)):
+                return
+            path = str(Path(args[0]).absolute())

+def require(value, reason):
+    if not value:
+        raise ValueError(reason)
+
+
+def digest(raw):
+    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+
+
+def strict(raw):
+    def unique(pairs):
+        result = {}
+        for key, value in pairs:
+            require(key not in result, 'duplicate JSON key')
+            result[key] = value
+        return result
+
+    def finite(value):
+        number = float(value)
+        require(math.isfinite(number), 'nonfinite JSON number')
+        return number
+
+    def invalid(value):
+        raise ValueError('nonfinite JSON constant: ' + value)
+
+    return json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_float=finite, parse_constant=invalid)
+
+
+def safe(name):
+    return (isinstance(name, str) and bool(name) and not name.startswith('/')
+            and all(part not in ('', '.', '..') for part in name.split('/'))
+            and str(PurePosixPath(name)) == name)
+
+
+def unpack(raw, expected):
+    require(sum(item['bytes'] for item in expected.values()) <= 16 * MIB, 'archive expansion bound')
+    files = {}
+    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw), mode='r:gz') as stream:
+        for entry in stream:
+            require(safe(entry.name) and entry.name in expected and entry.name not in files,
+                    'unexpected or duplicate archive member')
+            identity = expected[entry.name]
+            require(entry.isfile() and entry.size == identity['bytes'], 'archive member kind/size')
+            data = stream.extractfile(entry).read()
+            require(len(data) == identity['bytes'] and digest(data) == identity['sha256'],
+                    'archive member digest: ' + entry.name)
+            files[entry.name] = data
+    require(files.keys() == expected.keys(), 'missing archive members')
+    return files
+

+class Packet:
+    def __init__(self, directory):
+        self.manifest = strict((directory / 'manifest.json').read_bytes())
+        manifest = self.manifest
+        require(manifest['schema_version'] == 'shardloom.native_join_count.packet.v1', 'packet schema')
+        require(manifest['baseline_head'] == HEAD, 'baseline revision')
+        require(manifest['status'] == 'mechanism_comparison_passed_package_acceptance_pending',
+                'package status overclaim')
+        expected = {}
+        for identity in manifest['files']:
+            name = identity['path']
+            require(safe(name) and name not in expected, 'invalid or duplicate file identity')
+            require(type(identity['bytes']) is int and 0 <= identity['bytes'] <= 16 * MIB,
+                    'file size bound')
+            require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}', identity['sha256']), 'invalid SHA256')
+            expected[name] = identity
+        require(len(expected) == 374, 'frozen packet member coverage')
+        require(sum(item['bytes'] for item in expected.values()) == manifest['raw_member_bytes'],
+                'raw byte total')
+        archive = manifest['archive']
+        require(archive['path'] == 'packet.tar.gz' and 0 < archive['bytes'] <= 16 * MIB, 'archive path/size')
+        path = directory / archive['path']
+        require(path.stat().st_size == archive['bytes'], 'archive size')
+        raw = path.read_bytes()
+        require(digest(raw) == archive['sha256'], 'archive SHA256')
+        self.files = unpack(raw, expected)
+        require({name for name in self.files if not name.startswith(
+            ('join-count-comparison-r1/', 'join-count-observations-r1/'))} == AUXILIARY_FILES,
+            'auxiliary evidence coverage')
+
+    def raw(self, name):
+        if name.startswith(ORIGINAL):
+            name = name[len(ORIGINAL):]
+        require(safe(name) and name in self.files, 'missing evidence: ' + name)
+        return self.files[name]
+
+    def read(self, name):
+        return strict(self.raw(name))
+
+    def linked(self, reference):
+        raw = self.raw(reference['path'])
+        require(digest(raw) == reference['sha256'], 'linked evidence digest')
+        return raw

+def schedule(mode):
+    if mode == 'observe':
+        return [(case, role, 0, 0) for case in ROWS for role in ('baseline', 'candidate')]
+    result = []
+    for cohort in (1, 2):
+        for case in ROWS:
+            for sample in (1, 2, 3):
+                first = sample != 2 if cohort == 1 else sample == 2
+                roles = ('baseline', 'candidate') if first else ('candidate', 'baseline')
+                result.extend((case, role, cohort, sample) for role in roles)
+    return result

+def check_receipt(packet, name, status='passed'):
+    receipt = packet.read(name + '.json')
+    raw = packet.raw(name + '.log')
+    require(receipt['status'] == status and receipt['returncode'] == (0 if status == 'passed' else 101),
+            'build/test outcome: ' + name)
+    require(receipt['head'] == HEAD and digest(raw) == receipt['log_sha256'], 'build/test identity')
+    require(receipt['direct_child_reaped'] and receipt['process_group_drained']
+            and not receipt['timed_out'] and receipt['interrupted_signal'] is None,
+            'build/test supervision')
+    return receipt, raw.decode()

+def check_manifest(packet, manifest, role, mode):
+    directory = 'baseline-runtime' if role == 'baseline' else 'candidate-runtime-r1'
+    label = 'release' if mode == 'measure' else 'observe'
+    require(packet.read(f'{directory}/{label}-manifest.json') == manifest, 'runtime manifest identity')
+    require(manifest['revision'] == HEAD and manifest['features'] == ['release-user-surfaces'],
+            'runtime build/features')
+    require(manifest['profile'] == ('release' if mode == 'measure' else 'ci-native'), 'runtime profile')
+    require(manifest['harnesses'] == {HARNESS: HARNESS_SHA}, 'shared harness identity')
+    require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}', manifest['binary_sha256']), 'binary digest')
+    require(manifest['binary'] == ORIGINAL + directory + '/shardloom-join-count-' + label,
+            'runtime binary path')
+    source = manifest['source_inventory']
+    require(len(source) == (2126 if role == 'baseline' else 2129), 'runtime source coverage')
+    require(source[HARNESS] == HARNESS_SHA, 'source harness identity')
+    for name, sha in source.items():
+        require(safe(name) and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}', sha), 'source identity')
+    overlay = manifest['source_overlay']
+    raw = packet.linked(overlay)
+    with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw), mode='r:gz') as stream:
+        members = {}
+        for entry in stream:
+            require(entry.isfile() and safe(entry.name) and entry.name not in members
+                    and 0 <= entry.size <= 2 * MIB, 'source overlay member')
+            require(entry.name in overlay['members'], 'extra overlay source')
+            data = stream.extractfile(entry).read()
+            require(digest(data) == overlay['members'][entry.name] == source[entry.name], 'overlay source identity')
+            members[entry.name] = digest(data)
+    require(members == overlay['members'] and len(members) == (4 if role == 'baseline' else 16),
+            'overlay coverage')
+    build = strict(packet.linked(manifest['build_receipt']))
+    receipt_name = manifest['build_receipt']['path'][len(ORIGINAL):-5]
+    checked, _ = check_receipt(packet, receipt_name)
+    require(build == checked, 'build receipt')
+    require(build['command'][:4] == ['cargo', 'test', '--offline', '--locked'], 'build command')
+    require(build['command'][build['command'].index('--features') + 1] == 'release-user-surfaces',
+            'build feature selection')
+    require('--lib' in build['command'] and build['command'][build['command'].index('-p') + 1] == 'shardloom-vortex',
+            'build target')
+    require(('--release' in build['command']) == (mode == 'measure'), 'build profile flags')
+    for name, sha in members.items():
+        require(build['changed_source_inventory'][name]['sha256'] == sha, 'compiled overlay identity')
+

+def inputs_and_answer(packet, root, case, record):
+    def witness(sha):
+        require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}', sha), 'witness identity')
+        raw = packet.raw(root + '/witnesses/' + sha + '.json')
+        require(digest(raw) == sha, 'witness bytes')
+        return strict(raw)
+
+    require(len(record['input_witnesses']) == 2, 'two complete inputs')
+    keys = []
+    for side, (sha, count) in enumerate(zip(record['input_witnesses'], ROWS[case])):
+        data = witness(sha)
+        require(set(data) == {'n', 's', 'id'}, 'input fields')
+        require(len(data['n']) == len(data['id']) == count, 'input cardinality')
+        require(all(type(value) is int for value in data['id'] + data['n']), 'input integer type')
+        require(data['id'] == list(range(count)), 'complete input IDs')
+        numbers = []
+        for row in range(count):
+            if case == 'duplicate_numeric': value = row % 64
+            elif case == 'composite_text': value = row % 32
+            elif case == 'skew': value = row + 1 if row % 10 == 9 else 0
+            elif case == 'tiny': value = row % 7
+            elif case == 'unique_no_match' and side == 1: value = row + count
+            else: value = row
+            numbers.append(value)
+        require(data['n'] == numbers, 'frozen numeric inputs')
+        strings = [f'clé-東京-{value}' for value in numbers] if case == 'composite_text' else []
+        require(data['s'] == strings, 'frozen text inputs')
+        keys.append([(number, strings[row] if strings else None) for row, number in enumerate(numbers)])
+    right = Counter(keys[1])
+    answer = sum(right[key] for key in keys[0])
+    require(witness(record['schema_witness']) == SCHEMA, 'authoritative output schema')
+    for field in ('expected_rows_witness', 'actual_rows_witness'):
+        value = witness(record[field])
+        require(isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 1 and set(value[0]) == {'rows'}
+                and type(value[0]['rows']) is int and value == [{'rows': answer}], 'independent complete values')
+    return answer, len(right)
+

+def number(text, name, separator=':'):
+    values = re.findall(r'\b' + re.escape(name + separator) + r'\s*(\d+)\b', text)
+    require(len(values) == 1, 'unique reported counter: ' + name)
+    return int(values[0])

+def check_record(record, case, role, mode, answer, unique):
+    require(record['protocol'] == 'native-join-count-v1', 'record protocol')
+    require(record['complete_values_match'] is True and record['complete_schema_match'] is True,
+            'record correctness status')
+    require(record['expected_rows_witness'] == record['actual_rows_witness'], 'complete result identity')
+    require((record['left_rows'], record['right_rows']) == ROWS[case], 'record input rows')
+    require(record['reserved_after_cleanup'] == record['denied_reservations'] == 0, 'record cleanup')
+    require(record['memory_grant_bytes'] == 128 * MIB and type(record['peak_reserved_bytes']) is int
+            and 0 <= record['peak_reserved_bytes'] <= 128 * MIB, 'native reservation grant')
+    for field in ('engine_execution_ns', 'preparation_ns', 'result_serialization_ns'):
+        require(type(record[field]) is int and record[field] >= 0, 'record clock')
+    runtime = record['runtime']
+    for field, expected in [('completed_executions', 1), ('provider_background_workers', 0),
+                            ('admitted_max_parallelism', 1), ('limit_bytes', 128 * MIB), ('denied_reservations', 0)]:
+        require(number(runtime, field) == expected, 'reported runtime: ' + field)
+    certificate = record['native_io_certificate']
+    require('schema_version: "shardloom.native_io_certificate.v1"' in certificate
+            and 'diagnostics: []' in certificate, 'native certificate')
+    fallback = re.findall(r'\bfallback_attempted:\s*(true|false)', certificate)
+    require(fallback and set(fallback) == {'false'} and 'fallback_execution_allowed: false' in certificate,
+            'no-fallback certificate')
+    require(number(certificate, 'scans_started', '=') == 2
+            and number(certificate, 'delivered_scan_rows', '=') == sum(ROWS[case]), 'complete source delivery')
+    activated = role == 'candidate' and case != 'ineligible_count_column'
+    counts = dict(zip(COUNTS, (int(activated), ROWS[case][1] if activated else 0,
+                              ROWS[case][0] if activated else 0, answer if activated else 0)))
+    if role == 'candidate':
+        for name, value in counts.items():
+            require(number(certificate, name, '=') == value, 'certificate mechanism counter')
+        require(number(certificate, 'counted_join_distinct_build_keys', '=') == (unique if activated else 0),
+                'certificate unique key count')
+    require(record['observation_enabled'] is (mode == 'observe'), 'instrumentation isolation')
+    if mode == 'measure':
+        require(record['observations'] is None, 'release observation contamination')
+    else:
+        observed = record['observations']
+        require(observed['join_output_rows_constructed'] == (0 if activated else answer), 'constructed pair count')
+        require(observed['join_retained_right_rows'] == (unique if activated else ROWS[case][1]),
+                'retained build rows')
+        for name, value in counts.items():
+            actual = observed[name] if role == 'candidate' else observed.get(name, 0)
+            require(type(actual) is int and actual == value, 'observed counted state')

+def comparison(packet, mode):
+    root = 'join-count-comparison-r1' if mode == 'measure' else 'join-count-observations-r1'
+    outcome = packet.read(root + '/outcome.json')
+    protocol = packet.read(root + '/protocol.json')
+    expected = schedule(mode)
+    require(outcome['complete'] is True and outcome['mode'] == protocol['mode'] == mode, 'comparison completion')
+    require(outcome['protocol'] == protocol['protocol'] == 'native-join-count-v1', 'comparison protocol')
+    require(outcome['schedule'] == protocol['schedule'] == [list(row) for row in expected]
+            and len(outcome['calls']) == len(expected), 'complete fixed schedule')
+    manifests = outcome['runtime_manifests']
+    require(manifests == protocol['runtime_manifests'] and set(manifests) == {'baseline', 'candidate'},
+            'runtime manifest selection')
+    for role, manifest in manifests.items():
+        check_manifest(packet, manifest, role, mode)
+    require(manifests['baseline']['toolchain'] == manifests['candidate']['toolchain']
+            and manifests['baseline']['toolchain'].startswith('rustc 1.99.0 '), 'identical compiler')
+    require(outcome['source_inventory_before'] == outcome['source_inventory_after']
+            == protocol['source_inventory_before'] == manifests['candidate']['source_inventory'], 'source freeze')
+    binaries = {role: manifest['binary_sha256'] for role, manifest in manifests.items()}
+    require(outcome['binary_sha256_before'] == outcome['binary_sha256_after'] == protocol['binary_sha256_before']
+            == binaries, 'executable freeze')

+# Native workflow drop evidence packet
+
+This packet preserves the three isolated Full43 observations for the dropped native workflow batch, their acceptance and supervision receipts, the runtime restoration receipt, and the independent reference. It is an offline audit artifact; `verify.py` reads the manifest and object-addressed `packet.tar.xz` without extracting files or executing ShardLoom.
+
+The verifier checks archive and per-file SHA-256 identities, safe regular tar members, duplicate JSON keys, exact one-pass query coverage, process cleanup and input stability, every completed gzip output, complete result values against the pinned reference, schema continuity, engine-time sums, the failed candidate regression gate, and restoration to current main. It reports engine totals as evidence only. It makes no causal attribution and does not claim that this dropped batch changed runtime behavior.
+
+Run from this directory:
+
+```sh
+python3 verify.py manifest.json packet.tar.xz
+python3 -O test_verify.py -v
+```
+
+The packet is bounded to 16 MiB per file and 96 MiB expanded. Query records retain engine time; supervised wall time and other diagnostic clocks are not presented as engine time. The packet does not establish completion of the dropped phase item, and placeholder output payloads are not evidence of real Vortex output.
+
+It contains 594 original files in 462 content-addressed objects: 20,317,793
+expanded file bytes and 2,634,588 archive bytes. Nine test methods include
+malformed JSON, mismatched identities, archive traversal/links/duplicates,
+bounded decompression, missing/duplicate queries, incomplete identity checks,
+altered engine times/result hashes, incomplete result payloads, fallback and
+changed retain/drop receipts. +"""Offline corruption controls; no engine execution or local evidence paths required."""

+class PacketTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.manifest = (ROOT / "manifest.json").read_bytes()
+        cls.archive = (ROOT / "packet.tar.xz").read_bytes()
+        cls.verifier = (ROOT / "verify.py").read_bytes()
+        cls.files = v.object_files(cls.manifest, cls.archive, cls.verifier)

+    def test_complete_packet(self):

+    def test_strict_json(self):
+        for raw in ('{"a":1,"a":2}', 'NaN', 'Infinity', '-Infinity', '1e999'):
+            with self.subTest(raw=raw), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                v.strict_json(raw)
+
+    def test_value_types_and_float_tolerance(self):
+        for a, b in ((True, 1), (1, 1.0), ({"a": 1}, {"b": 1}), ([1], [1, 2]), (1.0, 1.001)):
+            self.assertFalse(v.equivalent(a, b))
+        self.assertTrue(v.equivalent([1.0], [1.0 + 1e-13]))
+        for value in (True, -1, "-1", "1.0", "１", None):
+            with self.subTest(value=value), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                v.unsigned(value)
+
+    def test_manifest_and_archive_identities(self):
+        for changes in ({"expanded_file_bytes": 0}, {"unique_objects": 0}, {"files": []}):
+            meta = v.strict_json(self.manifest)
+            meta.update(changes)
+            with self.subTest(changes=changes), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                v.object_files(json.dumps(meta), self.archive, self.verifier)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            v.object_files(self.manifest, self.archive + b"x", self.verifier)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            v.object_files(self.manifest, self.archive, b"different verifier")
+
+    def test_archive_safety(self):
+        def reject(names, symlink=False):
+            stream = io.BytesIO()
+            with tarfile.open(fileobj=stream, mode="w:xz") as archive:
+                for name in names:
+                    entry = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
+                    if symlink:
+                        entry.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE
+                        entry.linkname = "/tmp/escape"
+                    archive.addfile(entry)
+            packed = stream.getvalue()
+            meta = v.strict_json(self.manifest)
+            meta["archive"].update(bytes=len(packed), sha256=v.sha(packed))
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                v.object_files(json.dumps(meta), packed, self.verifier)
+        valid_empty = "objects/sha256/" + v.sha(b"")
+        reject([valid_empty, valid_empty])
+        reject(["../escape"])
+        reject([valid_empty], symlink=True)
+        # A small configured ceiling tests the same bounded decoder without a huge fixture.
+        with patch.object(v, "MAX_TAR", 1024), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            v.object_files(self.manifest, self.archive, self.verifier)
+
+    def test_gzip_bounds(self):
+        with patch.object(v, "MAX_FILE", 32), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            v.bounded_gunzip(gzip.compress(b"x" * 33))
+        for raw in (gzip.compress(b"x") + b"trailing", gzip.compress(b"x")[:-1]):
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                v.bounded_gunzip(raw)
+
+    def test_summary_corruption_after_rebinding(self):

+        summary_key = v.normalized(original_driver["summaries"][0]["path"])
+        mutations = (
